title: Which breakpoint type fits this bug
purpose: Choose a breakpoint type from the symptom of a bug: known line, only some calls, no pause allowed, or an unknown line.
summary: A short deck about choosing a breakpoint type. The main path splits bugs into those where you know the line and those where you do not, then shows what to read at the pause. Two deep dives compare a logpoint with a conditional breakpoint and list the three DOM change breakpoint types.
explanation: A breakpoint type is a question you ask the browser: pause on this line, pause only when this is true, log without pausing, or pause when this event, request or DOM change happens.

learning_check.question: You need the value of q on every call but the bug disappears when the page pauses. Which type do you use?
learning_check.answer: A logpoint. It prints q in the Console on every call and never pauses, so the timing of the race stays the same.

slides.heading: Which breakpoint finds this bug?
slides.notes: Ask the learner what they know about the bug before they choose a breakpoint type.

slides.heading: You know the line
slides.notes: Reveal each case. The three types all sit on one line of code and differ in when they stop.

slides.heading: You do not know the line
slides.notes: When the line is unknown, pause on the cause: a request, a DOM change, an event or an exception.

items: A changed node: DOM change breakpoint
A click or key: event listener breakpoint

slides.heading: Then read the pause
slides.notes: At every pause, read Scope for the values and the Call Stack, including the async frames, for the callers.

items: Async frames: who started the wait

slides.heading: Choose the closest pause
slides.notes: The best breakpoint stops closest to the cause, so you read the state before it changes again.

slides.heading: Log or pause on a condition
slides.notes: A conditional breakpoint pauses only when its expression is true; a logpoint never pauses and prints its message in the Console.

left.label: Conditional breakpoint
items: Pauses when the condition is true
You read Scope and Call Stack

right.label: Logpoint
items: Prints to the Console on every call

visual.verdict: Log when pausing changes the timing.

slides.heading: Three DOM change breakpoints
slides.notes: In the Elements panel you choose which change pauses: a child changes, an attribute changes, or the node is removed.

items: Node removal: the node is removed
